clue.text: Cast off from small lake in Ireland

the Irish word for a lake or sea inlet, as in Lough Neagh

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast off' looks like a boating phrase, but it is the verb for a snake shedding its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To slough is to shed dead skin or a covering, as a snake does, so it means discard.

clue.text: Plant from garden I pulled up

explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden flower with tall spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Listened to one-time neat group on the radio

clue.text: Flipping sauce by American close to Taylor Swift

clue.text: Abandoning son, Italian gentleman departs unnoticed

clue.text: Draw large aquatic mammal back to quay

parts.note: its final letter

clue.text: Butter providing nourishment for kids?

clue.text: Come across claims European's given parking penalty notice?

clue.text: Weak movies promoting filth essentially unknown

clue.text: Bold of a French journalist to host adult party
